name: How to Use PF2e Tavern Games

text.content:
How to Use PF2e Tavern Games

Open the game library

Enable PF2e Tavern Games, then use the dice button in Token controls, the PF2e Tavern Games button on an eligible character or NPC sheet, or the Open PF2e Tavern Games macro in the compendium. The GM chooses Poppy’s Prize from the existing table or opens the Tavern Games library to start Golem, Bounder, Century, or a Drinking Contest.

Participants and player panels

The GM selects eligible PC and NPC actors. For the card games, each player should have Owner permission on their actor. A player then opens their panel from their actor sheet or Token controls; the GM may use Open player panel on a table participant to prompt it remotely. The player panel contains only that actor’s private cards and legal controls. The GM retains final authority and may disqualify a participant from any game.

Game preparation

Golem requires three to six participants, Poppy’s Prize requires two to four, and Bounder, Century, and Drinking Contest accept two or more. The GM enters stakes using pp, gp, sp, and cp fields where relevant, then selects a Dealer or Shooter. Start buttons prepare a game; the designated Dealer or Shooter performs the first game action from their private panel or the GM table.

Cheating items

The module checks item slugs. A Poppy’s Prize or Golem dealer with marked-playing-cards may use marked cards. In Bounder, a Shooter with games-loaded-dice chooses their d20 result; in Century, the Dealer with that slug chooses the twenty results. A drinking contestant can elect to cheat when becoming Ready: the Fortitude save succeeds automatically, while the blind Performance check risks detection against every other contestant’s Perception DC.

Drinking Contest effects

The contest assigns and updates temporary PF2E conditions and a module-owned timed effect for each stage. Starting another drinking game or closing the contest clears effects created by the module; conditions that existed before the game are restored to their original values. Stage 6 sets unconscious for eight hours and removes the actor from the contest.

Results and reset

Every game maintains a shared activity log. Use Close table to clear the current multi-game state. Closing a drinking contest also clears its module-owned contest effects. Resetting does not reverse any currency changes that a GM has performed manually or through the original Poppy’s Prize automatic-currency option.

Source acknowledgement. Poppy’s Prize originates in Jewel of the Indigo Isles. Golem, Bounder, and Century originate in Pathfinder #159: All or Nothing, p. 76, as presented by Archives of Nethys. The drinking contest is a table rule supplied for this module.
